summary.text: Brenda Thiam is the Republican nominee for the Maryland House of Delegates, District 2B, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing incumbent Matthew Schindler (D).
A special education teacher, she represented District 2B in the House of Delegates from 2020 to 2023.
The Republican Party selected her as nominee after Sean Flaherty withdrew following his primary win.

paragraphs.text: Brenda Thiam was born in Pinehurst, North Carolina, and graduated from Hoke County High School.

She earned a bachelor's degree in physical education from North Carolina Central University in 1994, a master's degree in education from the University of Maryland, College Park, in 2002, and a Ph.D. in special education leadership from Capella University in 2015.
Her career experience includes working as a special education teacher, a behavioral health technician for Achieving True Self, and a director of education at the Community School of Maryland.
Thiam assumed office in the Maryland House of Delegates on September 23, 2020, and left office on January 11, 2023.

She was assigned to the Judiciary Committee, and in a Ballotpedia survey she said she served as minority whip and sponsored HB221, which became law in 2022 and provides disabled veterans with free angler's licenses.
She lost her 2022 re-election bid to Brooke Grossman, receiving 45.7% of the vote to Grossman's 54.2%.
In 2026 she sought the Republican nomination for Lieutenant Governor, finishing third with 6.4% in the primary.
In the survey, Thiam said she serves on the boards of Brook Lane Health Services and Meritus Health.
She lists public safety, improved educational outcomes including support for the B.O.O.S.T. scholarship program, and government accountability and responsible taxation as her main campaign messages.
